intro: Sidney anchors the northern end of the Miami Valley, about 36 miles up the Great Miami River from Dayton. Its 19th-century downtown core — the 1881 Shelby County Courthouse, the Monumental Building — is surrounded by early-1900s worker housing in one of the metro's older housing stocks. Stone foundations and aging roofs trap moisture: seepage through old stonework, slow roof leaks feeding attic mold, and a river-valley position that keeps ambient humidity high.
moldNote: Sidney's mold risk is age plus valley: 19th-century stone foundations that seep, aging roofs on worker housing, and river-valley humidity that slows drying after every rain.
